evidence.excerpt: Four commercial IP54-rated steel enclosures were instrumented with capacitive humidity sensors inside and outside, and temperature sensors at the wall mid-plane and external surface. They were mounted on a south-facing outdoor test rack in Novi Sad from March to October 2013. Internal relative humidity tracked external daily temperature cycles with a phase lag of approximately 3–4 hours. Total cumulative moisture ingress over the measurement period ranged from 4.2 to 7.8 g per enclosure, varying with seal type and mounting orientation. A one-dimensional transient diffusion model driven by measured vapour-pressure gradients reproduced the seasonal trend with a mean absolute error below 12 % when an effective diffusivity of 3.1 × 10⁻¹² m²/s was used for the compressed gasket region. The model indicates that horizontal lid orientation with a downward-facing seal gap reduces ingress by approximately 35 % compared with vertical orientation.
